# Open Instructional Systems — Full Specification

Version: 0.1.0-alpha
Generated: 2026-05-01T20:57:53.740Z

---

## What is OIS?

Open Instructional Systems (OIS) is a pedagogical design system — a set of tokens, patterns, and themes that describe instructional intent in learning materials. It gives instructors, platforms, and AI agents a shared vocabulary for the "how" of teaching, not just the "what."

---

## Tokens

### accessibility.mode
Category: accessibility
Type: enum
Definition: The primary accessibility design orientation of the learning experience.
Default: standard
Values:
    standard: Standard accessibility compliance (WCAG 2.1 AA).
    low-bandwidth: Designed to function in limited connectivity environments.
    screen-reader-first: Content is primarily designed for screen reader accessibility.
    multimodal: Content is available in multiple sensory modalities.
    flexible-deadline: Time-based constraints are minimized or eliminated.
    universal-design: Full Universal Design for Learning principles applied.

### accessibility.mediaAlternatives
Category: accessibility
Type: enum-multi
Definition: The accessible alternatives provided for media-based content.
Values:
    captions: Synchronized text captions for video or audio content.
    transcript: Full text transcript of audio or video content.
    alt-text: Text descriptions of images and visual content.
    printable: Print-ready versions of all materials.
    audio-description: Audio narration of visual information for video content.
    downloadable-assets: All assets available for offline download.

### agency.mode
Category: agency
Type: enum
Definition: The degree of learner choice and self-direction in the learning experience.
Default: bounded-choice
Values:
    fixed-path: The learner follows a predetermined sequence with no choices.
    bounded-choice: The learner chooses within defined options provided by the instructor.
    open-choice: The learner defines their own direction within the domain.
    self-directed: The learner sets goals, selects methods, and evaluates their own progress.

### agency.choicePoint
Category: agency
Type: enum-multi
Definition: The dimension(s) where learner choice is exercised.
Values:
    topic: Learner chooses what to study or investigate.
    tool: Learner chooses which tools or technologies to use.
    medium: Learner chooses the output format or medium.
    sequence: Learner chooses the order of activities.
    partner: Learner chooses collaborators.
    deliverable: Learner chooses the form of the final product.
    audience: Learner chooses who their work is for.

### aiUse.policy
Category: aiUse
Type: enum
Definition: The policy governing learner use of AI tools in this activity.
Default: not-specified
Values:
    prohibited: AI tools are not permitted in this activity.
    not-specified: No AI use policy has been defined. Not recommended for new content.
    permitted-undisclosed: AI use is permitted but disclosure is not required. Use sparingly.
    assisted-disclosed: AI assistance is permitted and must be disclosed.
    collaborative-disclosed: AI is used as a collaborative partner; disclosure and reflection required.
    experimental: Learners are explicitly using AI as the subject of investigation.
AI Guidance: Never set to anything other than prohibited without also setting aiUse.disclosureRequired to true.

### aiUse.allowedFunctions
Category: aiUse
Type: enum-multi
Definition: The specific AI functions permitted in this activity.
Values:
    grammar-check: AI may be used to check grammar and spelling.
    ideation: AI may be used to generate or expand ideas.
    drafting: AI may be used to draft text or outlines.
    research-assistance: AI may be used to find or summarize information.
    code-generation: AI may be used to generate code.
    image-generation: AI may be used to generate images.
    feedback: AI may be used to provide feedback on drafts.
    translation: AI may be used for translation.
    all: All AI functions are permitted.
AI Guidance: Be specific. List only permitted functions. Never leave unspecified when aiUse.policy is not prohibited.

### aiUse.disclosureRequired
Category: aiUse
Type: boolean
Definition: Whether learners must disclose their AI use in this activity.
Default: false

### aiUse.reflectionRequired
Category: aiUse
Type: boolean
Definition: Whether learners must submit a reflection on their AI use.
Default: false

### assessment.evidence
Category: assessment
Type: enum
Definition: The primary form of evidence collected to demonstrate learning.
Default: artifact
Values:
    quiz: A knowledge check or test with predetermined correct answers.
    artifact: A tangible product created by the learner.
    performance: A live or recorded demonstration of skill.
    portfolio: A curated collection of work over time.
    reflection: Written or recorded personal reflection on learning.
    critique-notes: Documentation produced during a critique or review session.
    process-documentation: Evidence of the learning process itself (sketches, drafts, logs).
    presentation: A structured presentation to an audience.
    artifact-plus-reflection: A finished product accompanied by a required reflection.

### assessment.mode
Category: assessment
Type: enum
Definition: The purpose or function of the assessment in the learning arc.
Default: formative
Values:
    formative: Assessment used to guide ongoing learning; low-stakes.
    summative: Assessment of learning at the end of a unit; higher-stakes.
    diagnostic: Assessment used to identify prior knowledge or gaps before instruction.
    ipsative: Assessment comparing learner to their own prior performance.
    mastery: Assessment that must be passed at a threshold before advancement.
    critique-based: Assessment conducted through structured group critique.

### collaboration.structure
Category: collaboration
Type: enum
Definition: How learners are organized for collaborative work.
Default: individual
Values:
    individual: Each learner works alone.
    pair: Learners work in pairs.
    small-group: Learners work in groups of 3-6.
    peer-review: Learners review each other's work in a structured exchange.
    studio-critique: Work is shared and critiqued in a group critique format.
    community-partner: Collaboration involves a real external community partner.

### collaboration.roleClarity
Category: collaboration
Type: enum
Definition: How explicitly roles are defined within collaborative work.
Default: none
Values:
    none: No role definitions given.
    informal: Roles emerge organically without formal assignment.
    assigned-roles: Specific roles are assigned by the instructor.
    rotating-roles: Roles rotate across activities or sessions.

### feedback.mode
Category: feedback
Type: enum
Definition: Who provides feedback on learner work.
Default: instructor
Values:
    none: No feedback is given.
    self: Learner evaluates their own work.
    peer: Another learner provides feedback.
    instructor: The instructor provides feedback.
    automated: Feedback is system-generated.
    community: Feedback comes from a community partner or external audience.
    peer-plus-instructor: Both peer and instructor feedback are provided.
    mixed: Multiple feedback sources are used.

### feedback.timing
Category: feedback
Type: enum
Definition: When feedback is provided relative to the submission or activity.
Default: after-submission
Values:
    before-submission: Feedback is given before the learner finalizes work (e.g., draft review).
    during-process: Feedback is given during the activity (e.g., coaching, in-process check-ins).
    after-submission: Feedback is given after the learner submits.
    iterative: Multiple rounds of feedback are built into the design.
    on-demand: Learner requests feedback when ready.

### localization.level
Category: localization
Type: enum
Definition: The depth of localization applied to the learning materials.
Default: none
Values:
    none: No localization. Original language and examples only.
    language-only: Text is translated but examples remain from the original cultural context.
    examples-localized: Both language and examples are adapted to the target cultural context.
    culturally-adapted: Deeper cultural adaptation including values, norms, and local context.
    community-co-designed: Materials were co-designed with members of the target community.

### bandwidth.assumption
Category: localization
Type: enum
Definition: The assumed internet connectivity level for learners.
Default: medium
Values:
    low: Assumes limited or intermittent connectivity (< 1 Mbps).
    medium: Assumes moderate broadband connectivity.
    high: Assumes reliable high-speed internet.
    offline-capable: All materials must function without internet access.

### reflection.required
Category: reflection
Type: boolean
Definition: Whether structured reflection is a required component of the learning activity.
Default: false

### reflection.focus
Category: reflection
Type: enum-multi
Definition: The subject or lens of the required reflection.
Values:
    process: Reflecting on how the learner approached the task.
    concept-transfer: Reflecting on how concepts apply to other contexts.
    creative-choice: Reflecting on aesthetic or design decisions made.
    ethical-use: Reflecting on ethical dimensions, especially AI use or community impact.
    collaboration: Reflecting on how the group worked together.
    failure-analysis: Reflecting on what didn't work and why.
    metacognition: Reflecting on one's own learning and thinking strategies.

### revision.required
Category: revision
Type: boolean
Definition: Whether learners are required to revise their work after feedback.
Default: false

### revision.mode
Category: revision
Type: enum
Definition: The structure of the revision requirement.
Values:
    optional: Revision is available but not required.
    required-once: One revision cycle is required.
    required-until-proficient: The learner must revise until meeting the proficiency threshold.
    iterative-cycle: Multiple structured revision cycles are built into the design.

### scaffolding.level
Category: scaffolding
Type: enum
Definition: The degree of instructional support provided to the learner.
Default: medium
Values:
    none: No scaffolding. Learner must self-direct entirely. (use when: Expert learners only.)
    low: Minimal prompts or guiding questions only. (use when: Intermediate to advanced learners with prior domain knowledge.)
    medium: Some structure, examples, or guiding questions provided. (use when: Mixed experience levels; most adult learners.)
    high: Worked examples, templates, checklists, and step-by-step guidance. (use when: Novice or early-stage learners; high-stakes tasks.)
    adaptive: Scaffolding adjusts dynamically based on learner progress. (use when: Platforms with adaptive learning capabilities.)
AI Guidance: Match scaffolding level to learner experience. Beginners need high; advanced learners benefit from low to build agency.

### scaffolding.type
Category: scaffolding
Type: enum
Definition: The primary modality of instructional support provided.
Values:
    worked-example: A solved problem or completed example provided for reference.
    checklist: A list of steps or criteria the learner can check off.
    template: A partially completed structure for the learner to fill in.
    guided-steps: A sequential set of instructions that walk the learner through the task.
    exemplar: A high-quality example of a finished product for comparison.
    coaching: Ongoing feedback from an instructor or peer throughout the process.
    none: No scaffolding type. Used with scaffolding.level none.
AI Guidance: Use in combination with scaffolding.level. If scaffolding.level is high, specify the scaffolding.type so AI agents can generate the right support materials.


---

## Patterns

### observe-analyze-create-critique-revise
A studio-based cycle where learners study exemplars, analyze structure, make original work, receive critique, and revise.
Problem: How do you design a learning experience where making, feedback, and revision are the core of learning — not supplemental?
Sequence:
  1. Observe
     Learner: Study 2-3 exemplars of finished work in the target form.
     Instructor: Curate exemplars that represent the range of quality and approach. Prompt observation with guiding questions.
  2. Analyze
     Learner: Identify patterns, techniques, decisions, and what makes each exemplar effective or not.
     Instructor: Facilitate structured analysis using a common vocabulary or rubric.
  3. Create
     Learner: Produce original work in response to the brief.
     Instructor: Circulate, offer coaching feedback during process.
  4. Critique
     Learner: Present work to peers; receive structured feedback using established criteria.
     Instructor: Facilitate critique. Model feedback language. Keep critique focused on work, not person.
  5. Revise
     Learner: Revise work based on critique. Document what changed and why.
     Instructor: Review revision with attention to responsiveness to feedback.
AI Guidance: When generating materials for this pattern, produce both a student-facing brief (phases 1-5 as instructions) and a studio critique guide for the instructor. Ensure the exemplars section specifies what to observe. Do not skip the revision phase.


---

## Themes

### constructivist-studio
A making-centred pedagogical style where learning happens through creating, critiquing, and revising work.
Token Defaults:
  scaffolding.level: medium
  agency.mode: bounded-choice
  feedback.mode: peer-plus-instructor
  feedback.timing: before-submission
  assessment.evidence: artifact-plus-reflection
  assessment.mode: formative
  revision.required: true
  revision.mode: required-once
  reflection.required: true
  reflection.focus: process
  collaboration.structure: studio-critique
Preferred Patterns: observe-analyze-create-critique-revise, peer-review-studio-cycle, constraint-based-project-sprint
AI Guidance: When generating materials for this theme, foreground making. The project brief should lead with the deliverable and the critique structure, not a reading list. Include a studio critique guide. Reflection should focus on process and creative choices.

## Validation Rules

### objective-requires-evidence [error]
Learning Objective Requires Assessment Evidence
If: assessment.evidence
Then: assessment.evidence must be present
Message: No assessment evidence type is specified. Every learning activity must define how learning will be evidenced.
Rationale: Without a defined evidence type, there is no basis for evaluating whether learning occurred.

### revision-requires-timely-feedback [error]
Revision Requires Pre-Submission Feedback
If: revision.required in [true]
Then: feedback.timing
Message: revision.required is true but feedback.timing is after-submission. Revision cannot be meaningfully performed without timely feedback.
Rationale: If feedback arrives only after submission, learners cannot revise in the same cycle.

### ai-use-requires-disclosure [error]
AI Use Requires Disclosure
If: aiUse.policy not in [prohibited, not-specified]
Then: aiUse.disclosureRequired must be [true]
Message: aiUse.policy permits AI use but aiUse.disclosureRequired is not set to true.
Rationale: Any non-prohibited AI use must require disclosure for academic integrity.

### ai-collaborative-requires-reflection [error]
Collaborative AI Use Requires Reflection
If: aiUse.policy in [collaborative-disclosed]
Then: reflection.required must be [true]
Message: aiUse.policy is collaborative-disclosed but reflection.required is not true. Collaborative AI use requires reflection.
Rationale: Collaborative AI use involves the highest degree of AI integration. Without reflection, learners cannot develop critical AI literacy.

### low-bandwidth-needs-alternatives [warning]
Low Bandwidth Requires Downloadable Alternatives
If: bandwidth.assumption in [low, offline-capable]
Then: accessibility.mediaAlternatives must include [downloadable-assets]
Message: bandwidth.assumption is low or offline-capable but no downloadable-assets media alternative is specified.
Rationale: Low-bandwidth learners need downloadable assets to access content offline.

## Implementation Recipe

1. Fetch /ois-index.json
2. Identify learning goal, learner level, domain, constraints
3. Select theme from themes
4. Select pattern from theme.preferredPatterns
5. Resolve tokens (theme defaults → pattern requirements → local overrides)
6. Run validation rules
7. Generate materials using pattern sequence
8. Output transparency summary
9. Output machine-readable pedagogy block
10. Return to user with validation report
